Persistence works — the order survives a reload, and Settings sets it too. Open **http://maker:4001** and confirm:

1. Change the **Sort** dropdown to **Title A–Z**. Now **reload the page** — it comes back sorted A–Z instead of resetting. Your choice is remembered.
2. Click **⚙ Settings**, set **My default order** to **Oldest saved**, and **Save**. Reload again — it opens in Oldest-saved order.

One assumption I want to be upfront about: I made the **toolbar choice and the Settings default the same remembered preference** — so changing the dropdown *is* changing your remembered default, and Settings is just an explicit place to set it. 

The alternative some apps use is to separate them: a *temporary* sort for the current session that snaps back to a *fixed* default next time. I went with the simpler "it just remembers what you last picked."

(In this prototype "remembered" uses your browser's local storage; in the real app it would be tied to your personal account so it follows you.)

**Does the "it remembers your last choice, and Settings lets you set it explicitly" behaviour match what you meant — or would you prefer temporary sorting kept separate from a fixed default?**
